title: VeRA shared scaling codes vs Mirror scaling views
hypothesis: Orbit-coded VeRA tasks can be represented by one shared scale vector plus low-description Mirror angles at lower serialized bytes; unrelated scale codes need private state.
physical_object: One shared frozen rank-4 A/B basis
mirror_coordinate: One task-specific angle rotating the first two scale coordinates

development.selection_metric: test MSE and actual serialized payload bytes

optimization.code_fit: least squares and nonlinear least squares for Mirror chart

storage.serializer: uncompressed NumPy NPZ, native learned dtype; Mirror base code and angles packed into one array before fresh access
paid_objects: packed Mirror base code and per-task angles in one coordinate array

compute.active_compute_proxy: dense projection and rank reconstruction MAC proxy; code decode operations reported

success_gate: At least 3/4 fresh aligned worlds: Mirror MSE <=1.10x VeRA, <=80% VeRA bytes and below hard tying.
failure_gate: Mirror aligned MSE >1.25x VeRA on >=3/4 seeds, or <10% byte reduction at matched quality.
